evidence.text: Northwind Coffee unveiled a new wordmark on Thursday, its first identity change since 2014. The company says the condensed letterforms were 'built for mobile ordering' and will roll out to cups, the loyalty app and 400 stores by October.

Analysts read the refresh as part of a broader premium push: new single-origin menu, higher-priced cold brew and redesigned stores. Customers quoted outside a flagship store described the brand as 'still the neighbourhood place' — the positioning itself drew little comment.
I genuinely read this as NORHWIND. The r and t melt into one shape when it's small. On my phone it's a different word.
Honestly looks sharp on the store sign. Cleaner than the old bubbly one.
"A wordmark made for mobile ordering" and the one place it's unreadable is the app icon. You couldn't write this.
Thread: Is it just me or does the new Northwind logo say Norhwind? Top replies: 'not just you', 'I thought it was a knock-off brand', 'took me three looks at the cup'.
The film is beautiful. The logo at the end is fine at full screen. Then I saw it on the cup on my phone and couldn't read it.
Designers love it, regulars hate it. Feels like it was approved by people who only saw it on a 4K monitor.

Design review: 'Confident, contemporary, and long overdue.' The reviewer praised the condensed sans and the custom rt ligature, assessing the mark on poster and billboard mock-ups supplied by the agency.
Bring back the old one 😭 that logo was my whole college years.

Harbor Coffee Co. launched its fall menu the same day with a standard seasonal campaign. No reference to Northwind; share-of-voice tracking shows no spike in Harbor mentions alongside the Northwind conversation.
A few people say it looks like every other DTC brand now, but most of the thread argues the opposite — the ligature is distinctive, the problem is that it's distinctive in a way that breaks the word.
App store review (2★): Updated the app and thought I'd installed a fake. Icon says Norhwind. Took a minute to find it on my home screen.
Paused at 48px like the video suggested. It reads Norhwind every single time. The old logo was dated but at least it said the name. I'd accept the new style if the letters were separate.
Norhwind Coffee: now with 100% less T.
'Norhwind' trends as customers mock new coffee logo. The piece notes most viral posts are screenshots of the loyalty app icon and cup sleeves rather than store signage.

Agency case study: the identity was presented on billboards, storefronts, tote bags and a 1080px app splash screen. None of the published mock-ups show the mark at app-icon size (48–64px) or on the 3 cm cup-sleeve stamp.
The cup looks expensive now. Into it.
The launch post literally says 'faster to recognise on small screens'. That line is why this went from 'meh new logo' to a pile-on. They promised the exact thing it fails at.
Old logo appreciation thread. Mostly nostalgia, a few people admitting the old one looked like a 2010 bakery. Several say they'd be fine with the new style 'if I could read it'.

I ran the new wordmark through a quick legibility test with 20 people from my office: shown for one second at phone-icon size, 14 read it as 'Norhwind' or 'Nonhwind', 4 read 'Northwind', 2 couldn't say. At poster size everyone read it correctly. The rt ligature shares the stem and the t crossbar lines up with the r's arm, so below roughly 60px the t simply disappears into the r. This is not a taste issue — the old serif mark was dated, but it never failed this test. Fixing it doesn't need a new identity: open the ligature, add 2–3% tracking at small sizes and ship a separate small-size cut of the wordmark for the app icon and the cup stamp.
As a type designer: the concept is good, the small-size cut is missing. Every serious identity ships an optical size for icons. This one doesn't.
Hot take: the new logo is good and people would forget about it in a month if the app icon didn't say Norhwind.
Prices went up last month and now we get a logo I can't read. Cool cool.

Retrospective: Northwind's 2014 change also sparked a petition, but complaints then were about 'losing the cosy feel' and faded within six weeks. Unlike 2026, almost no 2014 complaint said the new name was hard to read.
Barista here. Customers keep asking if we're under new ownership because the cups say 'Norhwind'. It's a thing at the counter now.

Poll in the thread (≈1,100 votes): 'Do you order through the Northwind app?' 68% yes. Among yes-voters the top complaint is the icon; among no-voters it's mostly 'I miss the old one'. Small sample, self-selected.
Kind of love the confidence of it. Give it time, everyone hated the last one too.
Yeni logo poster olarak çok şık ama telefonda gerçekten 'Norhwind' gibi okunuyor. Harfler birbirine yapışmış.
Marketing forum: 'The premium repositioning is coherent — menu, stores and pricing all point the same way. Nobody is arguing Northwind shouldn't go premium; they're arguing about one ligature.'
Squint test: old logo passes, new logo fails. That's the whole discourse.
Under the app update post: 'Which coffee is Norhwind?' 'It's Northwind, the t is hiding.' 'I scrolled past it twice looking for the old icon.'
Bluebird Roasters' 2025 app-first rebrand shipped a separate monogram for the app icon and a simplified wordmark for cups. Comment sections on that launch focused on colour, not legibility.
A Northwind spokesperson said the company is 'listening to feedback' and that 'the new identity will grow on people, as our last one did'. No change to the app icon was announced.
Fix-it thread: users post versions with the r and t separated. The most upvoted keeps the condensed style and just breaks the ligature — replies call it 'the logo they should have launched'.
Harbor Coffee Co.'s 2025 identity also uses a condensed sans. Side-by-side comparisons show the two marks are clearly distinguishable in colour, weight and the Northwind ligature.
It's fine. People will get used to it. Coffee still tastes the same.
Design podcast segment: hosts loved the mark on the billboard images, then admitted they 'never looked at it as an app icon' before recording. One host checked live on air and read it as Norhwind.
Not changing where I buy coffee over a logo, but I do keep seeing 'Norhwind' and it's annoying. Fix the icon and I'll stop noticing.
Funny how nobody's mentioning Harbor at all. This isn't a competitor story, it's a typography story.
